_about: Hand split of dataset20v3 papers into claims, by reading each paper's abstract/contributions against its reference experiments. C0 is the existing v3 claim. keep = distinct testable claim with its own headline experiment(s); thin = real claim but a single experiment or no numbers. Buckets: method_internal = tunes/ablates the authors' own method (unreachable by a proposer, since claims withhold the method); analysis = descriptive/diagnostic with no claim of its own; ungradeable = qualitative, no counts. 'shared' experiments (apparatus) appear in several claims. scope_flags = places where I disagree with scope.json for C0.

claims.draft: Training a model to resist deployment-style prompting does not make it resist activation steering: steering keeps eliciting deployment behaviour at every stage of that training, while prompts lose their effect.

A deployment-vs-evaluation steering direction taken from the untrained model shifts context-dependent behaviour beyond the trained organism: a naturally occurring marker, and a separately trained simpler organism.

A proactive face watermark trained on one dataset and a fixed pool of deepfake generators keeps recovering its source identifier, and stays imperceptible, on a held-out generator and on an unseen face dataset without retraining.
One shared decoder serving detection, localisation and tracing needs fewer parameters than dual-decoder forensic systems at the same payload length.

Model-level backdoor screening of prompt-tuned CLIP still catches backdoors from an adaptive attacker who narrows the trigger's activation region, and backdoors stored in the image encoder rather than the prompt module.
Backdoor triggers can be reconstructed from unlabeled out-of-distribution images nearly as well as from in-distribution data.

In adversarial training, shrinking the perturbation applied to correctly classified samples near the decision boundary barely changes the robustness learned, while shrinking it on samples far from the boundary destroys robustness.
The accuracy-robustness gains carry over from l-infinity to l2 threat models.

scope_flags: [5] compares the mean of clean and robust accuracy with nine published methods - exactly C0's 'exceeds the strongest prior' bar. scope.json marks it not required; it should be required.

claims.draft: Conventional visual backdoors fail to implant in VLA policies because benign and backdoor gradients conflict during fine-tuning; removing that conflict is what lets a backdoor take hold.

Existing defenses - input preprocessing, parameter pruning, safety layers and backdoor detectors adapted to continuous control - do not reliably remove a semantic-trigger backdoor from a VLA policy without heavy false positives.
Poisoning perturbations crafted on public proxy encoders transfer to the target VLA.
Localized parameter edits are amplified along low-variance directions of a language model's representation space, and that amplification tracks the decline of editing quality over sequential edits.
No knowledge-editing approach is best on both edit time and inference latency: parameter edits add no inference cost, external memory edits faster but costs at inference.

For agentic circuit explanation, an explicit observe-hypothesize-causally-validate workflow produces better explanations than the same agent skipping observation or validation, or working unstructured with the same tools.

When language-model agents fail at circuit explanation, the failure lies in validation rather than hypothesis formation: hypotheses are mostly grounded in observations, while validation plans are incomplete, code fails, and hypotheses stay unresolved.
Agentic circuit explanation transfers from semi-synthetic transformers to a circuit localized in a naturally trained LLM.

The safety signal that survives a successful jailbreak is sustained by a distinct set of mid-layer attention heads, and the heads that are suppressed are suppressed specifically by the jailbreak-template tokens rather than by the harmful request.

Training a general prover on automatically formalized geometry transfers: it improves proof success on a held-out competition set never used in training, and the same recipe improves a second, different prover.
Multimodal instruction tuning strengthens the causal role of the features tied to spatial reasoning.
A flat-object grasping system trained in simulation keeps its generalization to unseen objects and categories on a physical robot.
The multi-instruction gains hold at a larger model scale.
Small models trained to counteract exploration bias match much larger off-the-shelf models on multi-instruction benchmarks.

Existing in-context imitation policies for VLAs adapt poorly because their context retrieval matches visual appearance rather than behaviour and the policy's actions barely depend on the retrieved context.
A multimodal LLM can tell recoverable from state-breaking manipulation failures, and name the object to reset, from execution video.
A vision-language navigation agent trained only on standard continuous-VLN data transfers to a different navigation dataset and task, and to a physical robot in an unseen workspace.

For hazard awareness under partial observability, a planner must remember relationships among previously seen objects: full image history, retrieved text descriptions, or a bare list of seen objects do not preserve it.
Long-term environment memory still improves safe planning when the scene is fully observable.

scope_flags: [7] measures task success with hazards removed, which is C0's 'task success at least as high as an unmodified planner' clause. scope.json marks it not required; it should be required.
